more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.overview: Nisin is a preparation of closely related antimicrobial polypeptides produced by Lactococcus lactis bacteria. Its preservative role is to limit spoilage caused by microorganisms and extend the storage life of the food. Produced by fermentation with Lactococcus lactis strains. Nisin is a mixture of closely related antimicrobial peptides. The specified material is supplied as white powder.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain unripened cheese excluding products falling in category 16; ripened cheese; other creams; desserts excluding products covered in categories 1, 3 and 4; processed eggs and egg products.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.origin: Produced by fermentation with Lactococcus lactis strains. Nisin is a mixture of closely related antimicrobial peptides.
